chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sālim, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, what do you say regarding a woman who is on a journey with men among whom there is no mahram for her, and there is no woman with them, then the woman dies—what is to be done with her?

He عليه السلام said: Of her, that which Allah has made subject to tayammum is to be washed, and she is not to be touched, nor is anything of her beauties to be uncovered—those which Allah has commanded to be concealed.
So I said to him: How is that to be done with her? He عليه السلام said: The inner sides of her hands are washed, then her face is washed, then the outer sides of her hands are washed.

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمَ: dry ablution; here indicating the body parts corresponding to tayammum
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel or journeying away from home
key_terms.بَطْنُ كَفَّيْهَا: the inner side of the two hands
key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: a male relative permanently unmarriageable to her
key_terms.ظَهْرُ كَفَّيْهَا: the outer side of the two hands
key_terms.مَحَاسِنِهَا: the parts of her beauty or bodily features that must remain covered
key_terms.يُغَسَّلُ: is to be washed in the prescribed manner

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a woman dies while traveling with unrelated men and no other woman is present to wash her?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for the case of a woman who dies while traveling among unrelated men, with no mahram and no other woman present. It instructs that only the parts involved in tayammum are to be washed, without touching her body or uncovering what Allah has commanded to be concealed. The report is significant in fiqh for combining the requirements of funeral preparation with the obligation of modesty.
